# dsh-compaction-guard
> **If this helps you, please give it a star** — it helps others find it. Thanks!
Compaction integrity for DeepSeek Harness (dsh).

Long sessions compact; the compacted range takes constraints with it — "never
commit to main", "必须先跑

测试" — and the agent silently forgets rules it was
told to keep. This plugin watches `compaction/summ

ary` session events: it
extracts directive lines from the user-authored events being shadowed,
verif

ies each against the summary (**verbatim**, whitespace-normalized, or
**in substance** — a coverage

threshold on content words), and reports every
constraint the agent just forgot — console plus a dur

able JSONL ledger.
Pinned constraints from config are verified on every compaction. Zero LLM
calls i

.
Pinned constraints from config are verified on every compaction. Zero LLM
calls in the trust path.

Family channel #9: read / write / do / call / leave-behind / egress / told /
running / **remembered
— what the agent forgets**.
## Why now (checked 2026-10-17)

The awesome list has 209 memory plugins and an entire compaction package
family in dsh itself — and

**not one verifies that constraints survive
compaction**. Memory plugins add recall; this audits los

s. The
`compaction/summary` event even ships `shadowedSeqs` (exactly what was
compact away) — the in
tegrity check is deterministic by construction.
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Honest limitations, on purpose:

- Word coverage tracks **words, not meaning** — a paraphrase with no shared
vocabulary counts as los

t (conservative direction: false alarm, not silent
loss). Synonym-aware matching would need embeddin

gs or an LLM, which this
family refuses to put in the trust path.
- Coverage is judged against the *

*single best-matching summary sentence**,
never pooled across the whole summary — an unrelated sente

nce's 'never'
cannot vouch for a directive it never carried (external review C03).
- **Polarity is b

ound per candidate**: a negative directive whose best
sentence dropped the negation — or a positive

directive flipped negative —
is judged lost-polarity, not kept.
- This guard reports and ledgers; it

does not re-inject lost constraints or
block compaction.

## Compatibility
- **DSH**: verified against the 0.2.x line (source snapshot 0.2.1-alpha.2); installs on any profile

via `dsh plugin add` (prebuilt `lib/`, no build approval).
- **Node**: >= 20 (CI matrix: Node 20/22/

24 on Ubuntu and Windows).
- **Disposable-profile evidence (2026-10-19)**: `dsh plugin --profile <fr
esh> add github:zhengqiuyang/dsh-compaction-guard` → installed in 30s; boot shows `[dsh-compaction-g
uard] active: …`; `dsh plugin --profile <fresh> remove dsh-compaction-guard` → dependencies cleared,
`dsh plugin --profile <fresh> remove dsh-compaction-guard` → dependencies cleared, bundles restored.
## Develop
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Roadmap

- `reinject` mode: steer the lost constraints back into the session after
compaction (default stays

observe — auto-injection deserves live testing
first)
- Post-compaction reassertion listener (a cons

traint restated after the
summary also counts as survived)
- Turn-boundary constraints (task briefs
in the first turn pinned per-turn)
## Kill criteria

If dsh ships first-party compaction-integrity verification, this freezes at
its last working version
with a postmortem here.
## Known limitations
- **Word coverage tracks words, not meaning.** A paraphrase with no shared vocabulary counts as lost
(conservative: false alarm, not silent loss). As of this release, a negative directive ("never…") w
hose summary **drops the negation** is explicitly judged `lost-negation` instead of silently survivi

ng coverage.
- **This guard reports and ledgers — it does not re-inject lost constraints or block co
mpaction.** Restating the rule to the agent is your call; the report exists so you know you should.
- **Directive extraction is marker-based** (must/never/必须/…). Directives phrased without any marker
action is marker-based** (must/never/必须/…). Directives phrased without any marker are not collected.
